examInfo.format: Proctored multiple-choice exam. ServSafe says the exam has 90 questions: 80 are scored and 10 are unscored pilot questions mixed in. ServSafe's exam blueprint (based on its 2021 job task analysis) splits the 80 scored questions into seven content areas. Product listings describe the exam as 90 questions in 2 hours. This practice mock uses 80 questions with 4 answer choices and a 120-minute timer, following the seven content areas. All questions on this site are original AI-written practice questions; ServSafe does not publish its exam questions.

passCriteria.description: ServSafe's current FAQ says a passing score is 70% or higher, which means at least 56 of the 80 scored questions correct. An older ServSafe examinee handbook listed 75%, so check the score your proctor or state requires.

content.eligibility: Anyone can take the ServSafe Food Protection Manager exam. There are no education or work requirements. The exam must be taken with a proctor, either in person or through approved online proctoring. Many states and local health departments require a certified food protection manager in each food establishment, so check what your area requires.
content.intro: The ServSafe Food Protection Manager Certification is a food safety certification for managers and persons in charge in restaurants and other food operations. The exam checks whether you can run a kitchen that keeps food safe: managing food safety practices, hygiene and health, receiving and storage, preparation and cooking, service, cleaning and sanitizing, and facilities. ServSafe says the certification is recognized for five years, but state or local rules may set a different renewal period.
content.trendSummary: ServSafe's blueprint gives the largest share of scored questions to safe preparation and cooking (15 of 80), followed by receipt, storage, transportation, and disposal of food (13), and then hygiene and health, cleanliness and sanitation, and facilities and equipment (12 each). Management of food safety practices and service and display have 8 each. Expect many questions built on numbers: the 41°F to 135°F danger zone, cooking temperatures, two-stage cooling, reheating, the 7-day date-marking rule, and receiving temperatures. The temperatures and times on this site follow the U.S. FDA Food Code 2022.
content.studyTip: Make one card with every key number (41°F, 135°F, 145°F, 155°F, 165°F, 2 hours + 4 hours cooling, 7 days, 90 days for shellstock tags, 20 seconds handwashing) and review it daily. Then study the HACCP principles in order and the list of illnesses that must be reported. Finish with full 80-question mocks and aim for 64 or more correct.

faqs.question: How many questions are on the ServSafe Manager exam?
faqs.answer: ServSafe says the exam has 90 questions. Only 80 are scored; the other 10 are pilot questions used for research, and you cannot tell which ones they are. This site's mock uses 80 questions.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.answer: ServSafe's current FAQ says 70% or higher, which is at least 56 of the 80 scored questions. An older handbook said 75%, and some jurisdictions may have their own rules, so confirm with your proctor.

faqs.question: How long is the certification valid?
faqs.answer: ServSafe says it recognizes the Food Protection Manager Certification for five years. Your state, local health department, or employer may require renewal sooner.

faqs.question: Is this the same as the ServSafe Food Handler test?
faqs.answer: No. The Food Handler assessment is a shorter test for food workers. The Manager exam is a proctored certification exam for managers and persons in charge.

faqs.question: Are these real exam questions?
faqs.answer: No. ServSafe keeps its exam questions secure. Every question here is an original practice question written with AI from ServSafe's public exam information and the FDA Food Code, then checked by a separate AI review.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with Safe Preparation and Cooking of Food, the largest content area (15 of 80 scored questions), and learn its numbers first: the 41°F to 135°F danger zone, cooking temperatures, two-stage cooling, and reheating. Then study Safe Receipt, Storage, Transportation and Disposal of Food (13 questions), followed by Hygiene and Health, Cleanliness and Sanitation, and Facilities and Equipment (12 each). Finish with Management of Food Safety Practices and Safe Service and Display of Food (8 each), then take full 80-question mocks.
studyTips.hardChapters: Safe Preparation and Cooking of Food has the most numbers to keep apart: 165°F for poultry, 155°F for ground meat, 145°F for seafood and steaks, and 135°F for plant foods held hot. In Management of Food Safety Practices, practice the seven HACCP principles in order and tell a critical limit from monitoring, corrective action, and verification. In Hygiene and Health, learn which symptoms mean restrict and which mean exclude.
studyTips.examDay: ServSafe says the exam has 90 questions, but only 80 are scored and you cannot tell which 10 are pilot questions, so answer every question carefully. The current passing score is 70%, which is 56 of 80 scored questions. If two answers look right, choose the one that keeps food out of the 41°F to 135°F danger zone or that follows the stricter rule.
